{"data":{"repository":{"pullRequests":{"pageInfo":{"hasNextPage":false,"endCursor":"Y3Vyc29yOnYyOpK0MjAyNi0xMS0xOFQxMzozOTozMlrPAAAAAT_30Bc="},"nodes":[{"number":3342,"title":"feat(agent-links): permanent agent links on instar.sh/a (optional, off by default)","body":"## ELI16\n\nToday a link to something your agent has (a conversation, a document) points at one of the agent's computers. If that computer is away or its name changes, the link stops working, and an agent on two computers has two different links.\n\nThis adds an optional link that names **the agent itself**: `https://instar.sh/a#v=1&i=<agent id>&t=home|doc|conversation…`. The agent id is a fingerprint of the agent's own key. Everything after `#` stays on the device, so instar.sh stores nothing and never learns which agent or page a link is for. The Instar app finds the paired agent with that identity and opens the page over the agent's own Cloudflare or Tailscale connection, the same way it does today. A browser without the app gets a plain page with an \"Open in Instar\" button; nothing redirects.\n\nBefore the app trusts that a paired agent holds an id, the agent signs a fresh challenge with its identity key. The signature is tied to this phone and the address it used, so a second agent you've paired with can't claim to be the first one. A link only opens a page: it carries no password and grants no access.\n\nThe feature is off unless an agent's owner turns it on (`agentLinks.enabled`).\n\n## What changed in the code\n\n- `src/core/AgentLinks.ts`: the v1 link grammar (one parser, with accept/reject cases shared with the instar.sh page and the app), the link builder, a strict identity read, and the proof transcript and signature.\n- `GET /mobile/agent-link/identity` (`src/server/mobilePairingRoutes.ts`): device-signed and active-only; every person role may call it. It checks, in a fixed order, that links are on, that the nonce is valid, and that there is a verified host, then reads the identity and signs. It never mints, repairs or rewrites an identity, and records one evidence row per outcome.\n- `POST /agent-links` (`src/server/agentLinkRoutes.ts`, Bearer): builds links, and adds a `split-identity` warning taken from the identity-coherence check.\n- `agentLinks.enabled` config type and its live-read wiring in `AgentServer.ts`; awareness entry `src/data/awareness/agent-links.md`; ladder entry `agentLinks` (default off by preference).\n- instar.sh: a static `site/src/pages/a.astro` with the same-origin `site/public/a.js`. It makes no network request and never redirects. The Apple link file adds `/a` and `/a/` for the iPhone app and a new Mac app entry.\n\n## Why\n\nJustin (topic 141385, 2026-11-17 15:21) asked for a permanent link per agent that deep-links into the iPhone and Mac apps. It had to stay optional, keep using the agent's own Cloudflare or Tailscale network, and be secure. He approved the design (doc c101c6b8, topic 144473, \"approved\", 15:56 PT).\n\n## Review and approval\n\n- Design: Fable 5.2 and GPT 6 Astra each did a design pass on their own, then a cross-family security review. Both said not to redirect browsers through instar.sh, which would mean storing addresses and would hand phishers a trusted-looking forwarder.\n- Spec: `docs/specs/permanent-agent-links.md`, converged after 6 rounds (`docs/specs/reports/permanent-agent-links-convergence.md`). GPT 6 Astra raised no design findings in the last two rounds. Approved under Justin's design approval; not a constitution change.\n- Side effects: `upgrades/side-effects/permanent-agent-links.md`. Tier 2. About 23 files, about 1,700 lines including tests and the spec. Six review rounds is more than usual for the size; the reason is that this is an identity proof and a public link format.\n- Split out: the existing `/doc` page's script never runs, and reviving it would make instar.sh a forwarder. Filed as fb-f607b9d8-7d9.\n\n## Tests\n\n- Unit: `tests/unit/agent-links.test.ts`, 53 passing. Covers the grammar against the shared vectors, including a check that the instar.sh page parser agrees on every case; the builder; each refusal of the strict identity read; the nonce, transcript and proof; and the page and Apple-file checks.\n- Integration: `tests/integration/agent-link-routes.test.ts`.\n- E2E: `tests/e2e/agent-links-alive.test.ts`. It boots the production server, pairs a real phone, and checks the proof verifies over the phone's own transcript and fails for a different host; off gives `agent-links-off`. Not hand-run on the Studio, per the verify-line rule; Local Verify runs it.\n- Guard files and ratchets: run locally on this branch rebased on main (results in the PR thread).\n- App side (local app repo, branch `echo/agent-links`): 11 Swift tests pass, including the server-signed proof vector verifying in CryptoKit. The iPhone and Mac apps both build.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n","state":"OPEN","headRefName":"topic/144473-permanent-agent-links","baseRefName":"main","updatedAt":"2026-11-18T13:39:32Z","mergedAt":null}]}}}}
